name: S01 push: the first newline of the chunk, not the last
why: the lines after the first newline of a chunk wait in the tail until a later push, so a marker line that is the second line of its chunk answers one push late; run alone (runner, --bail 1), killed by the named case 'the same long line, the newline and the marker arriving together in the last chunk'

name: S02 push: the end of the completed text is one place too far
why: a chunk with no newline has `end` 1 and is cut, and the first character after a newline is tested with the lines and lost from the tail; run alone, killed by the first-answers row 'answers null while the newline of the URL line has not arrived, then the URL when it does' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S03 push: no +1, so a newline at index 0 reads as no newline
why: a chunk with no newline gets `end` -1 (not 0), a chunk that is only a newline gets 0 and is kept as a tail; run alone, killed by the helper row 'feed hands back every push's answer, the real scanner's and a stand-in's, and pushes each chunk once, in order'

name: S04 push: the no-newline test is `end <= 0`
why: EQUIVALENT: `end` is `lastIndexOf(...) + 1`, and `lastIndexOf` returns -1 or more, so `end` is 0 or more and `end <= 0` and `end === 0` are the same test (run alone with the runner: SURVIVES, as argued)

name: S05 push: a chunk that STARTS with a newline counts as having none
why: a chunk that is only a newline (end 1) is kept as a tail and answers null, so a URL line completed by a lone newline answers one push late; run alone, killed by the first-answers row 'answers null while the newline of the URL line has not arrived, then the URL when it does' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S06 push: the no-newline branch is taken for `end === 1`
why: a chunk with no newline goes through the completion path, which REPLACES the kept tail by the chunk, and a chunk that is only a newline is kept; run alone, killed by the first-answers row 'answers null while the newline of the URL line has not arrived, then the URL when it does' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S07 push: a chunk with no newline REPLACES the kept tail
why: the pieces received so far are dropped, so a line that arrives in three or more chunks is read from its last piece only; run alone, killed by the named case 'the live ANSI capture one character at a time' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S08 push: a chunk with no newline is put BEFORE the kept pieces
why: the pieces of a line are joined in reverse order; run alone, killed by the named case 'the live ANSI capture one character at a time' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S09 push: a chunk with no newline is parsed with all the pieces joined (the answer is the same, the cost is not)
why: the answer is the same (the joined tail has no newline, and a match needs one, so it is always null) but every push re-joins and re-reads the whole incomplete line: ONE line of 16 MiB in 4,096-character chunks and 256 KiB in one-byte chunks are quadratic again; run alone, killed by the clock rows only (13 s: the first clock row to run out of time)

name: S10 push: the kept text goes AFTER the new lines
why: the kept tail is appended to the completed lines instead of starting them; run alone, killed by the first-answers row 'answers null while the newline of the URL line has not arrived, then the URL when it does' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S11 push: the pieces are joined with a blank
why: a blank appears at every cut of the incomplete line, so a URL or an escape cut across two chunks is torn; run alone, killed by the named case 'the live ANSI capture one character at a time' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S12 push: the whole chunk is tested, not only up to its last newline
why: EQUIVALENT in the answer: the part of the chunk after its last newline has no newline, and a match ends on a newline, so it cannot start, end or extend a match; it is tested a second time later, when its own newline arrives, with the same result; the cost is at most one more read of each byte of a tail (run alone with the runner: SURVIVES, as argued)

name: S13 push: the last character of the completed text (the newline) is cut
why: the newline that ends every match is cut off, so nothing ever matches; run alone, killed by the helper row 'feed hands back every push's answer, the real scanner's and a stand-in's, and pushes each chunk once, in order'

name: S14 push: the first character of the new lines is cut
why: the first character of every chunk with a newline is lost; run alone, killed by the helper row 'feed hands back every push's answer, the real scanner's and a stand-in's, and pushes each chunk once, in order'

name: S15 push: the incomplete tail of a chunk is dropped
why: the text after the last newline of a chunk is lost, so a marker line that starts in one chunk and ends in the next is never seen; run alone, killed by the named case 'a marker line with the beginning of the next line in the same chunk, whose newline comes later'

name: S16 push: the tail is kept also when it is empty
why: EQUIVALENT: for `end === chunk.length` the kept piece is the empty string, and an empty piece joins to nothing (run alone with the runner: SURVIVES, as argued)

name: S17 push: a tail of one character is dropped
why: a chunk that ends one character after its last newline loses that character; run alone, killed by the E1 enumeration (a chunk cut one character after a newline)

name: S18 push: the kept tail starts one character late
why: the first character after the last newline is lost; run alone, killed by the named case 'a marker line with the beginning of the next line in the same chunk, whose newline comes later'

name: S19 push: the kept tail starts one character early, with the newline
why: EQUIVALENT: the kept text then starts with the newline that ended the last line, so the next completed text starts with one more EMPTY line; a match cannot start or end on an empty line, and a pattern with no anchor finds the same match, at the same place shifted by one (run alone with the runner: SURVIVES, as argued)

name: S20 push: a chunk that ends on a newline keeps the old tail
why: the pieces that were just tested stay and are joined in front of the next lines: a 'Browse at ' that ended a line is glued to the start of the next one (a false URL) and the cost grows with the stream; run alone, killed by the E1 enumeration and by a clock row (10 s)

name: S21 push: the tail starts with one empty piece
why: EQUIVALENT: an empty piece joins to nothing (run alone with the runner: SURVIVES, as argued)

name: S22 push: only the chunk is parsed
why: the kept tail is ignored, so a marker cut across two chunks is never seen; run alone, killed by the first-answers row 'answers null while the newline of the URL line has not arrived, then the URL when it does' and by a clock row's answer check

name: S23 push: only the new tail is parsed
why: the completed lines are not read at all; run alone, killed by the helper row 'feed hands back every push's answer, the real scanner's and a stand-in's, and pushes each chunk once, in order'

name: S24 push: a chunk with no newline is concatenated to the kept text at once
why: EQUIVALENT in the answer and in complexity, NOT in cost on every shape: the concatenation of strings is a rope in V8 and `join` of one element returns it unflattened, so no push reads the line, and the single flatten is at the newline, as before (run alone with the runner: SURVIVES, as argued). Measured with one fresh process each, `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` for the memory, load 7.3 to 9.2 read at the start of each process: ONE line of 4 MiB in one-byte chunks, the cure 139.8 to 143.0 ms and 196 to 197 MB, this mutant 322.9 to 332.8 ms and 241 to 242 MB (2.3x the time, 22% more memory); 12 MiB in one-byte chunks, the cure 427.8 to 439.5 ms and 551 MB, this mutant 952.2 to 975.4 ms and 601 MB (2.2x, 9% more); 3x the size gives 3.05x the time for the cure and 2.9x for the mutant, so both are linear; ONE line of 16 MiB in 4,096-character chunks, the cure 17.9 to 18.5 ms and 86 to 87 MB, this mutant 16.4 to 16.7 ms and 69 to 70 MB (0.9x, the mutant is a little faster and lighter there). The mechanism in the first sentence is the original argument and was not measured; the cost figures above were measured
